status: authored 2026-09-30 (the owner: "FERRY DOCKS: build the twelve. The charters exist on paper and docks are what make them real"). Nine of the twelve planned docks in data/ferries.json are sited and built here; three cannot be sited from any data in the repository and are listed under `not_sited` below with the decision each waits on. Generated by tools/ferry_docks.py into build/datapacks/cobblers_ferry_docks. NOTHING HERE HAS RUN IN A GAME: the functions are valid text that no server has executed.
source: data/ferries.json (the docks, their `near` and `near_basis`, and the lines that stop at them); docs/mechanics/WATER_PROPOSAL.md section 6 (the dock list); docs/world-building/FERRY_DOCKS.md (this build)
ground: tools/ground.py, rounded, and for a dock inside a settlement that does not stand on the heightmap, that settlement's own measured plan ground (tools/ground.py for_settlement). Never a world save: CLAUDE.md's ground rule, tests/test_ground_rule.py
style: spruce, after the docks already built: `first_cast`'s jetty (tools/route_events.py: spruce planks with stripped spruce wood grain, spruce log piles, a spruce fence rail, a step up at the shore) and the two Sunset piers in data/placements.json (planks at y64, log piles, fence rail, a lantern at the head). Deck height = the water level + 2, which is what all three already stand at. A twelfth dock in a new style would be worse than a plain one
spawn_blocks: tools/ferry_docks.py reads data/spawn_blocks.json and refuses any block a spawn condition names (data/system_contracts.json contract C4 lists the tools that must). Every block used here - spruce planks, stripped spruce wood, spruce log, spruce fence, spruce stairs, lantern - was checked against its 259 entries on 2026-09-30 and none is listed

not_sited.why: the water export removed the Jungle Isle (data/water_shape.json jungle_isle_bank) and the jungle ruins now measure y55-61 against a sea level of y62. There is no island to land on, its line `charter_jungle_ruins` is already `retired`, and docs/NIGHT_REVIEW.md review item 1 leaves the ruins' own home to the owner. A landing sited now would be sited on drowned ground

its `near` (1600, 8400) is outside the heightmap (z past 8191), so tools/ground.py cannot give it a ground at all, and WATER_PROPOSAL decision 8 builds nothing there until the client models and EXP-006 land
not sited in any data: Lugia's trench is Dive content (docs/world-building/WATER_MAP.md) and what a player stands on out there is undesigned. A dock needs a place to put its feet

docks.name: Pacifidlog jetty

host.why: the jetty is already built at the re-sited town: data/placements.json `sea_town_mainland_jetty` runs the bamboo spine from the plateau's south beach out to the landing at x5153-5167, z6654-6662, deck at the sea level y62 with its fences at y63 and lanterns at y64. This tool writes no block here: a dock does not rebuild another tool's jetty. It sites the ferryman and the landing on it and holds them honest

docks.landward: the bamboo jetty itself, 72 blocks north up its own spine to the plateau's south beach at (5160, 6586) - the town's one road out
docks.why: the Pacifidlog ferry's mainland end. The Sound jetty retired when the town moved (-2050, +420) on 2026-09-29; this is its replacement, and the landing the re-site already built is where a boat puts out

docks.name: Sunset West, the south pier

shore.why: the pier's own last dry column: south of z6633 the flats give way to water, which is why the pier was run out to z6639 in the first place

host.built_by: data/placements.json sunset_pier_south (an authored earthwork, re-apply R8)
host.why: the pier is already 50 columns of spruce deck at y64 from z6590 to z6639, with its piles, rail and head lanterns. The pier IS the dock's deck

docks.apron_why: the quay head goes WEST of the pier's landward root, not on it: x2699 is left as a gap so nothing this tool writes can touch the pier's own cells in data/placements.json. Boards are laid AT the ground (y63), not above it, so the heightmap ground under the ferryman is the ground the re-apply's audit reads
docks.landward: Sunset West's shore at y63, level ground the whole way from the quay head north-west into the town square at (2645, 6460)
docks.why: the Sunset strait's mainland end (WATER_PROPOSAL section 6 dock 6). The ferryman stands at the pier's root rather than its head because tools/ferries.py places and audits him on heightmap ground, and the head is 49 columns out over water - the same reason first_cast's boatman stands on the beach

docks.name: the Sunset isle

shore.why: the isle's north shore, 15 blocks from the dock's `near`: the nearest column whose whole 3-wide strip has open water straight north toward Sunset West and dry ground 6 columns back onto the isle

docks.landward: the Sunset isle's north shore at y62-63, walked south onto the isle itself; nothing else on the isle is built yet
docks.why: the Sunset strait's island end (WATER_PROPOSAL section 6 dock 10, which proposed about (2570, 6918); that point is 24 blocks inland of the shore the rule finds, and the jetty's head at (2572, 6880) lands on the dock's own `near`, the isle's land nearest the mainland). The strait is 255 blocks of water and knocks out every swimmer, so this dock is the only way on

docks.name: Sunset West harbour

shore.why: the west pier crosses 22 columns of flats before the water begins; this is the first column of real water under it, which is why the pier runs out to x2579

host.built_by: data/placements.json sunset_pier_west (an authored earthwork, re-apply R8)
host.why: the west pier into the river mouth's lee is already 52 columns of spruce deck at y64 from x2630 to x2579. The pier IS the harbour's deck

docks.apron_why: the harbour head sits EAST of the pier's root, landward of x2631, so nothing this tool writes can touch the pier's own cells. Boards at the ground (y63), bollards and lanterns at its four corners: the charters' home port needs somewhere to stand and something to tie to
docks.landward: Sunset West at y63, level ground east from the quay head into the town
docks.why: the charters' home port (WATER_PROPOSAL 4.3: 'Chartered travel from the harbour' is SQ-SUNSET-01's reward). Three $600 charters leave from here

docks.name: the north-east landing

shore.why: the dock's own `near` is the shore column the rule finds: marsh country's shore cell nearest the Pine Isles (contract C3 northlight_packet) is already dry with open water straight north

docks.landward: marsh country's shore at y62-64, rising south onto the marsh; the Northlight packet's mainland end has no road of its own yet
docks.why: the Northlight packet's mainland end (WATER_PROPOSAL section 6 dock 14). 388 blocks of water separate the Pine Isles from any mainland, so the packet is the only way across

docks.name: Northlight

shore.why: the dock's own `near`: South Pine Isle's shore nearest marsh country (contract C3) is dry, with open water straight south across the gap

docks.landward: South Pine Isle's shore at y62-65, rising north onto the isle toward the Northlight town plan in data/placements.json
docks.why: the Northlight packet's island end. It faces the mainland landing across the same water C3 measures

docks.name: Sabrina's town dock

water.level_source: data/legendaries.json uxie (the grotto mouth: 'the FIRST column at or below y59 (18 below the water level y77)'), measured on the applied water export

shore.why: Lake Tilpey's north shore below Sabrina's town: walking from the town's centre (6196, 3398) toward the lake's anchor (5870, 3874), the ground falls from y94 to the shore at y78 and the water begins at y77. The rule's column is the first whose whole 3-wide strip has open lake straight south

docks.landward: Lake Tilpey's north shore at y77-79, rising north 250 blocks to Sabrina's town at (6196, 3398); this is the shore the Dive school's north-shore sector is cut for (data/water_shape.json lake_tilpey)
docks.why: the Tilpey launch's first stop (WATER_PROPOSAL section 6 docks 11-13). The dock was never sited: data/ferries.json carried `near: null`, and this is the first time the shore under Sabrina's town has been measured for it

docks.name: the Weeping Elder

shore.why: the Weeping Elder island's north shore, on the line from its centre (5640, 4176; data/foliage.json weeping_elder_tilpey.site) toward the lake's anchor (5870, 3874) - the same line data/legendaries.json walks to site Uxie's grotto mouth. The jetty points back across the lake toward Sabrina's shore

docks.landward: the Weeping Elder island's shore at y77-80, rising south 65 blocks to the elder tree at its centre (5640, 4176)
docks.why: the Tilpey launch's island stop, EVT-G6-SLOWPOKE-FERRY. Never sited before (`near: null`); Uxie's grotto mouth is 30 blocks off this shore, which is why the island is worth a landing

docks.name: Tilpey's south shore

shore.why: Lake Tilpey's south shore. `near` is the lake's southern edge on the anchor's own meridian (walked due south from (5870, 3874) to the first dry column, y78); the rule's column is 23 blocks east of it, the nearest one whose whole 3-wide strip has open lake straight north

docks.landward: the lake's south shore at y77-78, walked south toward the outflow gorge and the southern coast road (data/towns.json: the route from Tilpey's south shore to Rift Foot)
docks.why: the Tilpey launch's far shore. Never sited before (`near: null`); the launch is a convenience across the lake, not a gate, and this is the end a player leaves for the gorge from
